# Metadata Standards

_SKOS concept in the [PKM Vocabulary](../)._

Characteristics or attributes of data are defined as properties and/or operations (methods or functions) for a common understanding of detail information with common names, data types, and allowed values, as well as relations to other objects.

**Also known as:** Metadata Schema

## Scope note

- Metadata is simply data about data. Metadata elements provide shared context and meaning; they are typically categorized as structural (machine readability), descriptive (for context), and administrative (for maintenance and lineage).
- Using standards for metadata schema helps to provide consistency and common semantics for metadata properties for concepts and relationships.

## Editorial note

_An open question about this term, not part of its definition._

The PKM namespace uses standard vocabularies and metadata from multiple standards:
- Dublin Core metadata (`dcterms`)
- SKOS (`skos`): schemes, concepts, and collections
- ISO 25964 (`isothes`): Thesaurus relations
- RDF Schema (`rdfs`): Resource Description Framework
- OWL (`owl`): Web Ontology Language
- FOAF (`foaf`): Linked Data — people and information (originally, "Friend of a Friend" from social web)
- Schema.org (`schema`): Standard web schemas
- Provenance(`prov`)
